alex_lee: ran the adaptive-sampler perf run on the microbatch scheduler this morning. saw weird noise where kernel selection seems to blame decode for ~30% of TTFT spikes. attaching short logs. :confused:

maria_g: can you paste the trace id / sample ids? curious if it's the same seq-length bucket.

alex_lee: trace id = trace-2026-03-18-01, sample ids 1023..1038. short dump:
```
SAMPLE 1023 seq=128 route=/api/chat model=gptx-3 microbatch=4 selected_kernel=fast_attn_v2 kernel_time_ms=1.2 decode_time_ms=0.8 ttft_ms=9.3 wait_ms=7.3
SAMPLE 1030 seq=512 route=/api/chat model=gptx-3 microbatch=8 selected_kernel=minimal_attn kernel_time_ms=0.5 decode_time_ms=2.9 ttft_ms=18.1 wait_ms=15.7
```

alex_lee: note: kernel_time small but wait_ms huge for some samples. suspicion: KV prefetch + scheduling handoff causes time attributed to `decode_time` because our probe fires before kernel handoff. the kernel's exec_time ends up in a later trace span so attribution flips.

chrisw: ah yeah that's the kernel-handoff window I mentioned last week. we currently tag kernel span with `selected_kernel` at probe A (pre-schedule), but the real exec happens after batch coalescing. we should move the kernel_time probe to after the actual launch.

samir: quick diff idea: add `kernel_launch_ts` and emit `kernel_exec_duration` after launch completes. also attach `batch_id` and `batch_size` to every token-level trace. will help split decode vs wait.

maria_g: If we change probe points we need to update dashboards. the token-latency breakdown widget (`per_token_ttft_breakdown_v2`) expects decode/kernel/wait buckets from the old probe. will break charts.

alex_lee: proposal: 1) implement post-launch kernel_time probe (non-blocking) 2) add `batch_id` and `route` labels 3) rollout only on canary for 24h 4) update atlas query to join by `batch_id` and recompute decode attribution.

perf-bot: automated-profile: canary rollout started on `canary-3` at 2026-03-18T01:15Z. sampling rate 0.5% across all routes. baseline p50 token TTFT=6.4ms, p95=21.8ms. instrumented-run p50=6.3ms, p95=20.9ms (preliminary).

chrisw: also let's add an adaptive sampler tweak: bias recording toward sequences with heavy KV hits (seq>256 && kv_hit_ratio>0.6) and to routes with recent p95 regressions. that should surface intermittent long tail.

alex_lee: sample tagging snippet I pushed to gist:
```json
{"trace_id":"$TRACE","sample_id":"$SAMPLE","batch_id":"$BATCH","route":"$ROUTE","kernel_selected":"fast_attn_v2","kernel_launch_ts": 1712345678}
```

maria_g: for dashboards I'll add two new panels: `kernel_launch_offset` and `batch_size_vs_ttft`. quick SQL-ish for atlas:
```
select route, batch_id, percentile(0.95, kernel_exec_duration + decode_time) as p95_ttft from token_traces where rollout = 'canary-3' group by route, batch_id
```

samir: question: are we okay with slight additional overhead for the post-launch probe? we can make it a lightweight counter emission (no extra allocations).

alex_lee: yes keep it minimal. disable body capture, only emit numeric durations and ids. if overhead > 0.2% we'll revert.

maria_g: I'll schedule a dashboard review tomorrow @9am PT. @chrisw can you add the adaptive sampler flags to the canary config?

chrisw: will do. adding flag `perf.adaptive_sampler.v2=true` and `perf.adaptive_sampler.bias_kv=true` to canary deploy.

perf-bot: notice: kernel_launch_probe enabled on canary-3 at 2026-03-18T01:22Z. collected 1.2k token traces so far. top routes: /api/chat (62%), /api/embeddings (18%).

alex_lee: thanks all. if the canary confirms reattribution fixes, we'll backfill p95 dashboards for last 48h and open a follow-up to tune batcher heuristics based on `batch_size_vs_ttft`. :thumbsup:

maria_g: :eyes: good plan. I'll create the follow-up ticket after the 9am review.

chrisw: adding note — might want to validate with synthetic replay too (highly regular seq lengths) to ensure we don't double-count kernel time.

samir: ok tagging perf-owners. I'm going to instrument a perf counter that emits `kv_prefetch_latency_ms` per batch so we can correlate.

alex_lee: great. thread done for now — will post results in this thread.
